key_insight: In this multi-institutional reader study, spectral deep learning reconstruction (DLR) generally matched or outperformed hybrid iterative reconstruction (HIR) for CT image quality across several body regions and both conventional and virtual monoenergetic images.
clinical_relevance: If confirmed in broader use, DLR could improve CT image quality while preserving diagnostic utility across multiple exam types derived from the same spectral CT data.
method: Retrospective post hoc analysis of 59 standard-resolution dual-layer spectral CT examinations from a larger blinded reader study.
Compared HIR (iDose4) versus spectral DLR (Spectral Precise Image) using conventional images and virtual monoenergetic images from identical raw data.
Two blinded radiologists or cardiologists scored randomized image pairs on a 5-point Likert scale with a model accounting for multiple readers per exam.
evidence_signal: DLR was noninferior and superior to HIR for head, abdomen, and cardiac exams, while chest conventional images were noninferior but not superior and chest VMI did not meet noninferiority.
watch_item: The analysis was limited to a smaller post hoc subset and chest VMI results were less clear, so broader validation and attention to potential ceiling effects are still needed.
paper_title: Deep Learning Reconstruction versus Hybrid Iterative Reconstruction for Spectral CT: A Multi-Institutional Image Quality Assessment
